answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a saffron merchant posting a bond at the market gate. The stake is tied to one verified work history, and any proven fraud slashes it, so creating a hundred fake lantern sellers costs a hundred bonds. Honest agents earn their stake back plus an opal-grade reputation that unlocks larger deals, making one trustworthy identity far more profitable than a swarm of disposable fakes.
